parameters.positive_direction: candidate favourable, matching the live candidate label
parameters.radius_formula: r(n) = sqrt((n + rho) * log((n + rho) / (rho * alpha_gate**2))) / n

decision_rule.evaluated_on: current full enrolled prefix n = N(t), at every look with n >= n_min
decision_rule.DEPLOY: L_hierarchy > 0 AND L_success > -delta, both at the SAME look
decision_rule.stopping: first crossing ends the trial; no retention of earlier crossings; no intersection over looks

cost_model.units: abstract cost units; the synthetic analogue of the live trial's latency_s
cost_model.pending_cost_enclosure: [ell, cost_cap]; the upper bound is the frozen resource cap and never narrows
cost_model.elapsed_accrual: an episode with final cost c and reveal offset D holds elapsed lower bound ell(a) = (c * a) / D at age a < D, and ell = c once a >= D; ell(a) < c for every a < D, so it is a valid lower bound, and it is nondecreasing in a
cost_model.evaluation_order_is_frozen: (c * a) / D, not c * (a / D); with integer c and a the numerator is exact, which keeps the tolerance boundaries reproducible

narrowing_thresholds.normative_form: the frozen predicate, evaluated as compare evaluates it: the pending arm can still be cheaper iff c - ell > atol + rtol*max(c, ell); the tie survives iff ell <= c or NOT (ell - c > atol + rtol*max(c, ell)). Re-derived in vband.cost_order_possibilities, not taken from the #11 monitor.
narrowing_thresholds.closed_form_reading: in exact arithmetic: the pending-arm branch dies at ell >= (1 - rtol)*c_revealed and the tie dies at ell > c_revealed/(1 - rtol)
narrowing_thresholds.closed_form_is_not_bit_identical: over the 2878680 (atom, revealed arm, d, age) states of the frozen delay grid the two readings disagree on exactly 128 states, all at the single point ell = c/(1-rtol) = 200/19 reached at elapsed fraction 5/19, where the predicate calls the tie infeasible and the closed form calls it feasible. The PREDICATE governs; sections 6.3 and 6.4 are computed with it. The 2878680-state sweep was run ONCE while writing this protocol (PROTOCOL 0.1 item 3) and is not re-run at fixture time: F17_atom_cost_table re-checks 47484 of those states, asserts that every disagreement it finds lies at elapsed fraction 5/19, and asserts that it finds exactly the 28 boundary states that grid reaches. It does NOT assert the full 128-state set; the corrected wording is PREREG_CHECK_2 N.3.
narrowing_thresholds.point_collapse_is_not_certified: a hierarchy enclosure that reaches a point this way has no final-score certificate, so certified stays false; see comparison_to_live_ab.certified_collapsed_scope

states.why: s_C = 0 makes the both-succeed branch infeasible, so the cost tier can never become eligible

states.cost_refinement: with c_C known and the incumbent pending in [ell, cap]: hierarchy is [-1, 1] while ell < (1-rtol)*c_C, then [0, 1], then the point [1, 1] once ell > c_C/(1-rtol)

states.why: s_I = 0 makes the both-succeed branch infeasible

states.cost_refinement: with c_I known and the candidate pending in [ell, cap]: hierarchy is [-1, 1] while ell < (1-rtol)*c_I, then [-1, 0], then the point [-1, -1] once ell > c_I/(1-rtol)

states.why: the certified collapse; the cost tier decides the BB atoms

enclosure_rules.protocol_2_5_rows_are_normative: The ten rows below are the machine-readable twin of the PROTOCOL 2.5 enclosure table, in its order, with its labels. Before PREREG_CHECK_2 N.2 that table was compared against nothing: cells.json was declared normative over the table that decides ground truth while no check read it. F15 now compares the two row for row, and also asserts that each row is consistent with the coarser `states` list above - the widest row of a cost-relevant state must equal that state's interval, every later row of the group must be a subinterval of it, and the success interval must not move within a group, because the cost tier cannot touch the success score.

protocol_2_5_rows.label: candidate revealed, s_C = 1, cost tie and incumbent-cheaper both still feasible
candidate revealed, s_C = 1, incumbent-cheaper infeasible, tie feasible
incumbent revealed, s_I = 1, cost tie and candidate-cheaper both still feasible
incumbent revealed, s_I = 1, candidate-cheaper infeasible, tie feasible

enclosure_rules.cost_rows_are_a_logical_consequence: Each cost refinement is the exhaustive enumeration of the feasible completions under the frozen predicate, and nothing more. The true score lies inside every row of this table at every elapsed value; verified by enumeration over every (atom, revealed arm, d, a) state.
enclosure_rules.point_is_not_certified: A hierarchy enclosure narrowed to a point by the cost tier while an episode is still pending is logically as tight as a resolved one but carries no final-score certificate, so certified = false and n_certified does not count it. The study reports both counts.

constructions.mean_over: all enrolled pairs 1..n, via their enclosures
constructions.target: mubar_n, the running conditional mean over the enrolled prefix

constructions.index: k = max{k : every pair 1..k fully resolved}
constructions.target: mubar_k, ITS OWN running target; NOT a bound on the current all-enrolled mean mubar_n
constructions.note: Under the i.i.d. laws of this study mubar_k = mubar_n = mu numerically, which is a property of these DGPs and not of the construction; this study cannot distinguish the two targets empirically.

constructions.index: m = |{j <= n : pair j fully resolved}|
constructions.mean_over: the outcome-selected completed subset C(n), which is NOT a prefix of the enrollment filtration
constructions.target: none guaranteed; no martingale argument applies
constructions.note: Included only to exhibit the failure mode and as the precommitted positive control of PROTOCOL.md 9.4. Must be labelled invalid in every table, caption and file.

no_speed_claim: No pathwise speed dominance is claimed for the latest-enrolled-prefix normal-mixture monitor, in either direction. The three constructions are evaluated at different indices on the same path; their decision prefixes are never presented as a paired speed statistic, a latency, or a saving.
coverage_target_boundary: Coverage validated here is for the BOUNDED ARBITRARY-RUNNING-MEAN target mubar_n = (1/n) sum_{i<=n} E[Z_i | F_{i-1}] of a synthetic stream. It does NOT establish the assumptions needed for a causal pair-orientation interpretation: pre-enrolled nonoverlapping arrival positions chosen without their outcomes, one fresh fair coin per pair logged and fsynced before either episode is dispatched, single exposure, no cross-pair interference, no dependence of a task's record on a later coin, an operator who does not act on coins, a fixed scheduling and resource policy, and the frozen outcome/missingness rule. A simulation assumes those; it cannot supply them.

outcome_atoms.sampling: k = rng.integers(0, 10000); frozen cumulative-threshold lookup in the order below (exact integer arithmetic)

definition.cost: equal costs, within relative tolerance 0.05: a tie

cost_columns.added_by: the pre-freeze revision, to close PREREG_CHECK B.6
cost_columns.Z_column_is_unchanged: every cost pair reproduces the frozen Z column exactly through src/winstats.compare with the frozen tiers; asserted by fixture F17_atom_cost_table
cost_columns.arm_exchangeability_of_L1_is_preserved: the arm swap maps BB+ <-> BB- and C>I <-> I>C with their cost pairs swapped, and fixes BB0 (40, 40) and FF (40, 40), so L1 remains an exact null in both gates and its expected band stays exactly symmetric
cost_columns.exact_threshold_equality: NOT placed in the grid, because a BB0 cost pair such as (38, 40) with |delta| = tol = 2.0 exactly would break the arm exchangeability of L1. The |delta| = tol boundary is exercised by fixtures F07 and F17 instead, and the tie branch of the ENCLOSURE boundary (ell = (1-rtol)*c exactly) is reachable in the grid whenever a/d hits it exactly.
cost_columns.why_these_magnitudes: 10 against 40 is decisive on the cost tier (tol = 0.05*40 = 2.0) and puts the pending arm's collapse threshold at an elapsed fraction of 0.2375/0.26316 of its own duration, so the cost enclosure path is exercised over most of a pending episode's life rather than in a sliver at its end; 40 against 40 exercises the tie branch, whose first threshold sits at an elapsed fraction of 0.95.

outcome_atoms.ground_truth_derivation: mu_h = (w[BB+] + w[C>I] - w[BB-] - w[I>C]) / 10000 ; mu_s = (w[C>I] - w[I>C]) / 10000. Exact enumeration over six atoms. Atoms are i.i.d. across enrolled pairs, so mubar_n = mu_h and nubar_n = mu_s exactly for every n on every path. Derived analytically, never by simulation. The cost columns do not enter this derivation: they reproduce the same Z column.

L1.name: aa_null
L1.description: A/A symmetric null; the atom table is invariant under exchanging the two arms, so the null is exact by construction and not only in expectation.

L2.name: pref_boundary
L2.description: Preference boundary with success favorable: mu_h = 0 exactly (least favourable for both the deploy hierarchy condition and the harm gate), mu_s = +0.25 so the success guardrail is genuinely true. A candidate that succeeds distinctly more often but is slower when both succeed.

L3.name: success_boundary
L3.description: Success boundary with preference favorable: mu_s = -delta = -0.03 exactly (least favourable for the guardrail), mu_h = +0.40 so the hierarchy condition opens early and a DEPLOY is governed entirely by a one-sided error of the success band at its exact boundary.

L4.name: favorable_alt
L4.description: The scientifically prespecified favorable alternative: a candidate both more successful and faster when both succeed. This is the only scenario in which the live study's T3 could deploy (protocol_FINAL 11.4); chosen for that reason, not for its rates.

delay_blocks.unit: enrollment ticks; pair i enrolled at tick i is fully resolved at every look with prefix n >= i + d_i

N.name: noninformative
N.description: d_i drawn independently of (Z_i, D_i) and of everything else.
N.sampling: u = rng.integers(0, 40000); long iff u < 3 * w_neg

A.name: outcome_dependent_asymmetric
A.description: d_i depends on the pair's own realized hierarchy score. Deliberately the strongest informative coupling in this family: the unresolved set is almost purely Z = -1. Chosen before any outcome existed, to make a failure of the completed-only rule detectable rather than to flatter the adapter.
A.sampling: for Z = -1: u = rng.integers(0, 4); long iff u < 3. Otherwise SHORT.
A.conditional_independence: given Z_i, d_i is conditionally independent of D_i and of every other pair

delay_rules.marginal_delay_matched: p_long(N) = (3/4) * P(Z = -1) is exactly the unconditional long-branch probability of rule A under the same law, so for each outcome law the N and A cells have identical marginal delay distributions, identical E[d], and identical expected unresolved and unrevealed fractions at every look. They differ only in WHICH pairs are slow.

partial_revelation.first_reveal_offset: f_i ~ DiscreteUniform{0, ..., d_i}, independent of the outcome given d_i
partial_revelation.first_reveal_arm: candidate with probability 1/2, independent of the outcome given d_i
partial_revelation.episode_durations: the first-revealed episode has duration f_i, the second d_i; both are dispatched at the pair's enrollment tick
partial_revelation.a_revealed_episode_is_final: its success AND its final cost are known at its own reveal offset

elapsed_cost_at_age_a.rule: ell = (c * a) / D for a pending episode of final cost c and duration D; ell = c once a >= D
elapsed_cost_at_age_a.emitted_for: every pending episode at every look, including before the first reveal
elapsed_cost_at_age_a.no_new_draws: deterministic given (atom, d_i, f_i, b_i); the five-array draw order of the seeding block is unchanged
elapsed_cost_at_age_a.only_cost_information: the elapsed lower bound and the final value. No cost upper bound below the cap is ever observed.

partial_revelation.declared_simplification_first_reveal_coi: In the live apparatus the faster arm tends to reveal first, which correlates with the cost tier; here the first-reveal identity is independent of the outcome given d_i. Declared because it makes partial information LESS adversarial in the cost direction than reality might be; the adversarial content of these cells is carried by the pair-level delay rule instead.
partial_revelation.declared_simplification_two_clocks: The cost meter and the reveal schedule are not tied to each other: an episode's final cost is fixed by its atom while its duration comes from the delay rule, so a cheap episode may reveal second. Declared. A latency-coupled model (cheap arm reveals first) would make the pending arm the expensive one and would therefore narrow the cost enclosure MORE often than this model does, so this choice is the conservative one for exercising the path, and it leaves the reveal schedule -- and therefore analytic_reachability.expected_unresolved_unrevealed_fraction -- unchanged by the revision.

no_cell_may_be_added: Exactly eight cells. No cell may be added, removed, reweighted or re-parameterized after any simulated outcome of this study exists, and in particular not after inspecting whether results are favorable.

1.note: discarded, never reused in the reported grid

seeding.namespaces_are_machine_checked: F15 compares the three ids, the sections each namespace names and the reuse column against the PROTOCOL 5 table, and compares the master seed against the two places PROTOCOL 5 writes it. Before PREREG_CHECK_2 N.2 that table was compared against nothing.
seeding.note: All five arrays are drawn unconditionally and at full length so the stream advances identically whichever branch a pair takes. Draw order is part of the seed's meaning; changing it changes every stream.

one_look_per_enrollment_prefix.taken_at: the state immediately before the next enrollment (maximal information at that prefix)
one_look_per_enrollment_prefix.justification: Within a fixed prefix n the band is nested-shrinking over looks, so miscoverage at any look at prefix n implies miscoverage at the last look at prefix n, and a decision firing at any look at prefix n also fires at the last look. This is an exact reduction of the all-triggers rule for ever-miscoverage and for the decision prefix tau, not an approximation.
one_look_per_enrollment_prefix.does_not_reproduce: the wall-clock instant of a decision; decision time is therefore reported in enrolled pairs only, never as latency

escalation.rule: 5,000 programs in the four boundary/delay cells only, precommitted here before any outcome
escalation.reading: the two boundary outcome laws under both delay rules; the alternative reading (two boundary cells plus two delay cells) was considered and rejected while writing this protocol, before any outcome existed
escalation.decided_by: the budget ladder from runtime and memory measurements alone; never by any effect comparison, coverage number or decision rate

resource_cap_endpoint_rule.unresolved_pairs: keep the enclosure they have and enter L and U through it
resource_cap_endpoint_rule.endpoint_if_no_crossing: NO_DECISION, recorded with the unresolved fraction at that look
resource_cap_endpoint_rule.why_drain_is_shorter_than_max_delay: max(LONG) = 699 > 200, so the endpoint genuinely carries unresolved pairs (1.56% to 3.51% in expectation), making the finalization rule a live rule rather than a formality

smoke_run.cell_choice_reason: C1 and C2 share the outcome law with the largest expected unresolved fraction among the non-escalating cells and differ only in the delay rule, so the pair measures both delay branches; under the section 9.1 all-looks reading every trial runs to the finalization look, so runtime is close to cell-independent and the split costs nothing.
smoke_run.forbidden: inspecting any effect column, coverage number or decision rate; the smoke run may not influence the horizon, cap, cells or any parameter

projection.scaling_exponent: measured, not assumed: beta = log(s_2000 / s_1000) / log(2) from the two smoke points, where s_H is seconds per program at horizon H
projection.peak_rss_projected: smoke_peak_rss (the run is batched; peak does not grow with the grid)
projection.why_it_is_measured: PREREG_CHECK B.7: one smoke point at a single N_max cannot measure the exponent, and per-look cost is O(1) only if the band is maintained incrementally. A recompute-per-look implementation is quadratic in N_max, under which the T4 row would be over-projected by a factor of two and the tier choice could be wrong.
projection.incremental_band_property: vrun.py must maintain the running enclosure sums incrementally (at most two enclosure changes per pair per look). vrun.py does not exist at the freeze commit; when it is written it carries an operation counter and asserts this property on the smoke run, before the grid starts, and the count goes into budget.json.

ladder.section_6_variant: analytic_reachability.T4_variant_N_max_1000, computed and deposited BEFORE the smoke run rather than recomputed after it
ladder.forfeits: the n = 2000 fixed-horizon summary required by root item 4; if T4 is selected the report states this as a reduction of the root's design

budget.selection_rule: the highest tier whose projection satisfies ALL of seconds_projected <= 5400, peak_rss_projected <= 2 GiB, bytes_projected <= 200 MiB; written to budget.json BEFORE the reported grid starts
budget.pause_and_report: if even T4 fails any of the three limits, the run PAUSES and reports; it does not silently shrink further, drop a cell, or reduce the number of constructions
budget.batching: by (cell, block of 100 programs); per-trial records appended to a gzip CSV incrementally; no per-look path is ever written to disk; peak RSS and cumulative output bytes are asserted after every batch

reported_quantities.wilson_caveat: These intervals quantify Monte Carlo error of this simulation only. They are not confidence intervals for the statistical guarantee, and a Wilson interval lying below a nominal level is not a proof that the level holds.

events.ever_miscover: exists look : mu_g < L_g(look) or mu_g > U_g(look)

per_gate_ever_miscoverage.evaluated_over: all looks to the finalization look, regardless of the decision, because the confidence-sequence guarantee is a statement for all n
per_gate_ever_miscoverage.secondary_column: the same restricted to n >= n_min

family_any_erroneous.event: at least one of the program's four trials has any_erroneous_trial

never_conjunct.event: L_h > 0 held at some look AND L_s > -delta held at some look, but never at the same look
never_conjunct.purpose: direct read-out that the same-look conjunction is doing work

timing_and_resolution.tau: the enrolled prefix n at the first look whose condition fired
timing_and_resolution.capped_decision_prefix: tau with tau := N_max for every non-deciding trial, by this explicit rule; Q1/median/Q3 over ALL trials, always printed with the capped fraction
timing_and_resolution.conditional_decision_prefix: Q1/median/Q3 of tau over deciding trials only, always printed with the deciding fraction
timing_and_resolution.unresolved_fraction: (n - #fully resolved) / n at the deciding look, or at the finalization look for non-deciding trials; mean and Q1/median/Q3
timing_and_resolution.unrevealed_fraction: the same with 'neither episode revealed' in the numerator
timing_and_resolution.cost_collapsed_fraction: the same with 'not fully resolved, and the hierarchy enclosure is a point' in the numerator: the measured counterpart of analytic_reachability.expected_cost_enclosure_exercise, and the read-out that makes the cost/latency enclosure path visible in the results rather than only in the design
timing_and_resolution.cost_narrowed_fraction: the same with 'not fully resolved, and the hierarchy enclosure is narrower than the success information alone would give' in the numerator
timing_and_resolution.certified_vs_point_counts: both are reported. A hierarchy enclosure narrowed to a point by the cost tier is a point WITHOUT a final-score certificate; n_certified counts only certificates, so the two counts differ by exactly the cost-collapsed pairs.
timing_and_resolution.forbidden: reporting decision prefixes as wall-clock, latency, throughput or saving, or as a paired comparison between constructions

reported_quantities.retention: Every unfavourable or inconclusive result is retained and reported. No cell, construction, gate or row is dropped, no row is omitted for brevity, and no run is repeated to obtain a different answer.

exceedance_flag.rule: FLAG iff the LOWER Wilson limit of the measured rate exceeds its nominal bound
exceedance_flag.unflagged_wording: reported as 'no exceedance was detected at this resolution', never as 'the bound holds'
exceedance_flag.flag_on_ADAPTER: a defect of the validated construction; reported under the disagreement procedure
exceedance_flag.flag_on_NAIVE_in_an_A_cell: the expected behaviour of an invalid rule; reported as the positive control, not as a defect

positive_control.statement: NAIVE's hierarchy ever-miscoverage must be FLAGGED in at least one of C2, C4, C6. If it is not, the measurement apparatus itself is reported as unvalidated, the ADAPTER results of this run are reported as uninterpretable, and the cause is investigated before any of them is cited.
positive_control.basis: the analytic expected-path arithmetic of PROTOCOL.md 6.2: the completed-only hierarchy band fails to contain the truth on the expected path from n = 202 in C2, n = 159 in C4, n = 365 in C6, and never in the N cells or in C7/C8
positive_control.gate: hierarchy only; no success-gate positive control is precommitted, because the omitted pairs carry D in {-1, 0} rather than a pure -1 and the success band is much less disturbed

analytic_reachability.status: exact expectations under the frozen law; no simulation; IGNORES sampling variability and is NOT a prediction of any reported rate
analytic_reachability.wording_rule: for this rule, this allocation and this grid; never a statement about what any method can or cannot certify
analytic_reachability.method: For each pair age a the enclosure state is enumerated over (atom, long/short branch, d, f, first-revealed arm) with its exact probability, giving E[lower] and E[upper] per age; the expected sum over a prefix is their partial sum, and the expected-path endpoint is that mean plus or minus r(n), clipped. P(f <= a | d) = (a+1)/(d+1). No random number is drawn anywhere in this section.

expected_unresolved_unrevealed_fraction.note: depends only on the reveal schedule (d_j and f_j), so the cost revision does not touch it; reproduced exactly by the recomputation
expected_unresolved_unrevealed_fraction.rounding: half-up at 4 decimal places; L4's 0.2308 and 0.1261 are the exact values 0.230750 and 0.126050

expected_path_gate_opening_prefix.effect_of_the_cost_revision: the L_h column opens earlier (C5 398->335, C6 169->160, C7 300->258, C8 145->137) because the cost tier now resolves part of the enclosure slack; the L_s column is IDENTICAL because the success enclosure is untouched, and the U_h<0 column is still never, which holds a priori since E[upper] >= E[Z] = mu_h >= 0 in every law

naive_expected_path_first_miscoverage_pr.note: NAIVE and CPREFIX read only fully resolved scores, so neither is affected by the cost enclosure revision

expected_cost_enclosure_exercise.what: [E fraction of the enrolled prefix that is NOT fully resolved and whose hierarchy enclosure the cost tier has collapsed to a POINT, E fraction that is not fully resolved and whose hierarchy enclosure the cost tier has narrowed at all]. The second contains the first. Both are zero under the pre-revision enclosure model, by construction: no partial state there could be narrowed by cost.
expected_cost_enclosure_exercise.why_it_is_here: it is the analytic evidence that the cells exercise the cost/latency enclosure path, which PREREG_CHECK B.6 found unexercised. Deposited before any outcome exists so that a later measured fraction cannot be presented as a discovery.
expected_cost_enclosure_exercise.reading: At n = 500 in C4, 5.50% of the whole enrolled prefix is a pair that no episode has finished resolving and whose hierarchy score the cost tier has nevertheless pinned to a point -- about a fifth of that cell's 25.99% unresolved fraction. At the finalization look of C1 the cost tier has pinned 0.77% of 2.92% still-unresolved pairs. The path is live in all eight cells at every horizon.

T4_variant_N_max_1000.why: budget tier T4 halves the horizon, so section 6 must be frozen for it too rather than recomputed after the smoke run; PREREG_CHECK B.8
T4_variant_N_max_1000.forfeits: the n = 2000 fixed-horizon summary required by root item 4; if T4 is selected the report states this as a reduction of the root's design, not as a budget detail

expected_path_gate_opening_prefix.note: identical to the N_max = 2000 table: the expected path at prefix n does not depend on the cap, and every opening prefix listed there is below 1000, so none is lost

deploy_route_unreachable_within_cap_in.reason: mu_s = 0 and r(n) < delta = 0.03 first holds at n = 17097, beyond the cap of 2000
deploy_route_unreachable_within_cap_in.wording: a PRE-SPECIFIED NEAR-CERTAIN ABSTENTION on the deploy route of those two cells, NOT a logical impossibility; if a DEPLOY occurs there it is reported as the rare event it is and never described as impossible
deploy_route_unreachable_within_cap_in.consequence: the decision-level probe of C1/C2 is the harm gate

analytic_reachability.primary_evidence_ordering: Because several decision-level probes are cap-limited or tail-limited, the primary evidence for each gate is the band-level one-sided ever-miscoverage, not the decision-level rate. Fixed now so a near-zero decision-level table cannot later be presented as if it were the strong result.
analytic_reachability.enclosure_conservatism_priced_now: In the A cells the unresolved pairs are the Z = -1 pairs, whose lower_j = -1 is tight while upper_j = +1 is maximally loose, so L_h is barely affected and U_h is inflated and the harm gate becomes much harder to reach. This is a correct and expected consequence of never imputing a pending outcome, stated before any outcome exists so it cannot later be reported as a discovery or as a defect. The cost tier relieves part of that inflation but does not remove it: in C2 the expected U_h at n = 500 is 0.4802 with the cost path and was 0.5695 without it, against a truth of mu_h = 0.
analytic_reachability.asymmetry_of_the_cost_path_stated_now: The cost tier narrows a partially revealed pair only when the REVEALED arm is the cheap one, because only then can the pending arm's elapsed cost overtake it. With the fair first-reveal coin this happens for about half of the cost-decisive pairs, and never for the other half. This is a property of the frozen reveal model, priced in the expected_cost_enclosure_exercise table above, and is not a defect of either implementation.

fixtures.register_is_machine_checked: F15 asserts that this list, PROTOCOL.md section 11 and vfixtures.ALL_FIXTURES carry the same ids in the same order. The pre-audit register named F0..F12 while the code implemented F01..F13; that mismatch is what this check exists to prevent.

list.assertion: identical physical arrivals with opposite pre-enrolled coins give opposite oriented scores; arm_slots follows the coin and not the arrival order; an outcome for an unenrolled position and an invalid coin are both rejected

at every look the divisor is exactly the enrolled prefix n, never the completed count, checked against a hand-computed four-pair table with resolved and unrevealed pairs; at n = 0 the full range is displayed and nothing decides

replaying every reveal three times leaves the state signature, the enclosures and the band endpoints bit-identical; a stale elapsed-cost report is an exact no-op; a conflicting second certificate raises
duplicate pair ids, reused arrival positions, self-overlapping pairs and facts for unowned positions are all rejected; enrollment positions are immutable and sequential
over all 720 reveal orders of the six episodes of a fixed three-pair stream the state signature and both bands are identical; the hand-derived sums, means and r(3) are reproduced

s_C = s_I = 0 gives Z = 0 and D = 0 with the cost tier never eligible even at a cost ratio that would be decisive; two observed failures pin both scores to 0 WITHOUT a certificate, so certified stays false

with relative_tolerance 0.05, cost 95.0 against 100.0 has |delta| = tol = 5.0 exactly and TIES (the decisive test is the strict |delta| > tol); 94.9 against 100.0 is decisive; both directions; the same boundary in the enclosure enumeration

a pair with neither episode revealed contributes exactly [-1, 1] to both scores; a single-arm reveal plus an elapsed-cost lower bound narrows exactly to its enclosure_rules row and no further; a point reached without a certificate is NOT certified; nothing is imputed

the cap is an explicit finalisation rule (failure at full cap), never a silent censor or drop; the capped pair stays in the ledger and in n; a timeout contradicting an observed success and a final cost above the cap are both rejected

at the traffic switch randomisation stops, in-flight pairs are still finished under their original assignment, post-switch single-arm traffic is logged as a follow-up cohort and never enters n, and the switch is idempotent

on a multi-look eight-look stream every pair's ultimately certified score lies inside EVERY bound that pair contributed at EVERY prior look, no enclosure ever widens, and the running-sum interval brackets the realised running mean at every look after enrollment closed

the alpha allocation, rho, delta and n_min; every locked radius against both vband.radius_from_formula and the independent literal transcription; an interior band at n = 2000 assembled as sum/n -+ r; the clip; that the prefix is a prefix; that a prefix beyond the ledger and a radius at n = 0 raise

DEPLOY iff L_h > 0 and L_s > -delta, RETAIN_INCUMBENT iff U_h < 0, both strict, both read at one look on one prefix, nothing below n_min; mismatched prefixes raise; deploy and harm never fire together

vband.radius_from_formula(n) equals the independent literal transcription of the guidance closed form with STRICT float equality for every n = 1..20000, and equals src/winstats.normal_mixture_radius(n, alpha=0.00625, rho=100., variance_process=n) likewise

the numeric tables of PROTOCOL.md listed here are parsed and compared to this file value by value, and nothing outside the list is claimed: the header provenance block (the three hash strings, the repository commit, the interpreter and numpy versions), 2.1 parameters and the alpha ladder, 2.2 radius reference values and the first-n-below sentence, 2.5 the enclosure-row table, 4 the cells, 4.1 atom costs, weights, ground truth and induced distributions, 4.2 the delay table with its denominator, 5 the seed namespaces and the master seed, 6.1/6.2/6.3/6.4 including their horizon headers, their law-and-delay row labels and the T4 variant, 7.1 the grid and the look counts derived from it, 8.2 the budget ladder including its per-cell grid column, 9.1 and 9.2 the nominal bounds and the numbers in their definitions, 9.3 the flag thresholds, 11 the fixture register and every F01..Fnn range printed in the document, and 13.0 the module map

importing vband, vfixtures and tests_validation in a fresh interpreter loads NO module whose __file__ is under experiments/live_ab/ or experiments/live_ab_validation/pinned/, and no source file of this directory except vcompare.py names either path

every atom's cost pair reproduces the frozen Z and D columns through src/winstats.compare; over 47484 of the (atom, revealed arm, d, elapsed age) states - the fixture's own delay grid, NOT the full 2878680-state sweep of PROTOCOL 2.5 - the cost enclosure narrows monotonically, never widens, always contains the true Z, and collapses to a point exactly at the frozen thresholds, and the 28 boundary states that grid reaches are asserted as a count so the check cannot pass by never reaching the boundary

every provenance pin is recomputed FROM THE FILE: src/winstats.py, the guidance document and the #11 vocabulary document named in this file's provenance block are opened and hashed with sha256 and compared against both this file and the hash strings printed in PROTOCOL.md, and the three sources in pinned/ are hashed and compared against pinned/PINNED.json, whose file list must be exactly the Python sources present there. A pin that no longer matches the file it names fails loudly; the string-to-string comparison this replaces could not see it (PREREG_CHECK_2 N.1)

comparison_to_live_ab.import_graph_test: no module reachable from the #12 band, enclosure, generator or fixtures imports anything under experiments/live_ab/ or experiments/live_ab_validation/pinned/; implemented as F16_import_graph_independence and tests_validation.TestImportGraphIndependence
comparison_to_live_ab.look_set: every look at prefix n = 1..N_max plus the finalization look. NO look is taken at n = 0 on either side: #12 displays the full range there and #11 raises, and that structural difference is named here rather than adjudicated later.

compared_at_every_look.decision_label: exactly equal under the frozen bijection below

map.plus_a_required_condition: the #12 trial must end in NO_DECISION; a #11 horizon_no_decision at a look where #12 returns DEPLOY or RETAIN_INCUMBENT IS a disagreement

decision_label_bijection.why_horizon_needs_a_rule: #12 has no horizon concept at all, so the #11 horizon branch has no #12 counterpart. Mapping it to CONTINUE at the look level and to NO_DECISION at the trial level is the only mapping under which both sides describe the same trial endpoint; it is fixed here so that whoever writes vcompare.py cannot choose it after seeing the streams.
decision_label_bijection.any_label_outside_this_map: is a disagreement, not an unmapped case

comparison_to_live_ab.exception_rule: An exception raised by either side at a look where the other side returns a value IS a disagreement. It is written to comparison_defects.csv with the exception type, the message, the side that raised, and the seed coordinates to replay it alone. It is never treated as a skip, a filter or a test-harness detail.

certified_collapsed_scope.in_scope: the per-pair enclosure ENDPOINTS, on both scores, at every look
certified_collapsed_scope.why: The two sides hold incompatible definitions. #12 marks certified only on a valid final-score certificate, so a hierarchy enclosure that the cost tier has narrowed to a point while an episode is still pending is a point that is NOT certified. PREREG_CHECK A.4 item 6 reports that #11 requires the flag to be true exactly when both scores are points and raises otherwise. Comparing the flag would therefore report a definitional difference as a numerical defect at every cost-collapsed pair, of which section 6.4 says there are many.
certified_collapsed_scope.not_silence: the difference is a NAMED, pre-registered finding: the report states it, states that section 4.4's cost path makes it common rather than exotic, states that neither reading is declared correct here, and escalates it with the rest of section 12.3.
certified_collapsed_scope.each_side_builds_its_own_state: vcompare.py drives both implementations from the same event stream and never constructs one side's objects from the other side's state, so neither side's constructor is fed a state its own rules forbid.

disagreement_policy.never: reconciled by editing either side - not the band module, not the enclosure rules, not the tolerance, not the fixture streams, not this protocol
reported_with: the guidance clause each side appears to implement
the seed coordinates to replay it alone
disagreement_policy.adjudication: escalated to the coordinator and the root; which side is wrong is NOT decided by this author
disagreement_policy.until_adjudicated: #11's results do not count as validated, and the report says so in those words
disagreement_policy.within_tolerance_but_systematic: reported as a noted numerical difference with its magnitude, not silently accepted
disagreement_policy.agreement_wording: 'the two implementations agree on these 200 streams to 1e-12', never 'the monitor is correct' - two implementations of the same misreading of the guidance agree perfectly, and this comparison cannot detect that

outputs.guard: any path outside that directory is refused and the run aborts rather than writing elsewhere
outputs.determinism: two runs produce byte-identical outputs apart from the timing fields of compute.json, asserted by re-running one cell block
outputs.report: experiments/live_ab_validation/REPORT.md, naming the validated adapter commit and file hashes from pinned/PINNED.json, with the limitations of PROTOCOL.md 1.3 repeated in full and not summarized away

change_control: This file and PROTOCOL.md are frozen on commit. Any change to a cell, parameter, seed, grid, estimator, reported quantity, flag rule or positive control is a new protocol version with its own freeze; results produced under the old version keep the old label and are reported beside the new ones rather than replaced. The budget tier selected by the ladder is not a change: it is an output of a rule this file fixes, recorded in budget.json.
